newsitem.title: CANADA: Bombardier has no regrets on jet deal.
newsitem.headline: Bombardier has no regrets on jet deal.

text.p: Bombardier Inc indicated on Tuesday that it had no regets on losing half of a $2.4 billion jet order from AMR Corp's American Eagle Airlines to Brazilian rival Embraer SA.

American Eagle said at the Paris air show on Tuesday that it had agreed to buy 42 50-seat jets from Embraer, with options for 25 more, and had agreed to firm orders for 25 70-seat Regional Jets from Bombardier's Canadair unit, with options for 25 more.

Bombardier officials told reporters that the Montreal-based Aerospace and transportation equipment manufacturer company could not compete with Embraer on pricing in the bidding for the 50-seat jet portion of American Eagle's order.

"We will not take on projects that do not meet our commercial requirements and also that will not allow us to provide sufficient return to the shareholders," Bombardier Aerospace president and chief executive Robert Brown said in a telephone conference call from the air show.
Brown went on to hint that state-owned Embraer may not make a profit on its winning bid for the 50-seat jets.
"I think it's very hard for people to meet the pricing requirements that were required here and to remain profitable in the future," Brown said.
During the conference call, officials from Bombardier and American Eagle declined to specify the pricing gap between the 50-seat jets being offered by Bombardier and Embraer.
The Canadian government and Brazilian governments are in talks under the auspices of the World Trade Organization on claims by Canada that Brazil is illegally subsidizing Embraer.

Brown said American Eagle's order for Bombardier's 70-seat jets would significantly boost the new plane's development program. The 70-seat jet is a stretch version of Bombardier's successful 50-seat Regional Jet.
With the American Eagle orders, Bombardier has accumulated 117 orders, options and memoranda of understanding on purchasing the 70-seat jet.
"We feel very confident, particularly with the start that we've got here, which is quite frankly much quicker than we had on the 50-seater,that we are going to have a successful program," Brown said.
On the Toronto Stock Exchange on Thursday afternoon, Bombardier Class B shares were at C$30.10, off five cents from Monday on a volume of more than 700,000 shares.
